Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

1	# Independent Fortress microGPT experiment — Fable-side blinded run
2	
3	This brief parallels the Astra-side assignment (branch `codex/astra-microgpt`,
4	`experiment/WORKER_BRIEF_DRAFT.md`) with only the changes this environment
5	requires. The point is a fair, comparable baseline: same mission, same
6	standard of success, same blinding discipline, different environment plumbing.
7	
8	## Mission and standard of success
9	
10	Find and justify a canonical, idiomatic Fortress expression of microGPT whose
11	executable, typeset definitions look as close as possible to the mathematics
12	used in transformer/ML papers. Put each mathematical formula beside its actual
13	rendered Fortress definition: the reader must be able to judge the
14	correspondence **by eye**. This visual and semantic correspondence is the
15	forcing function.
16	
17	The main article teaches two things together, with equal pedagogical weight:
18	how a GPT works, and how to construct the Fortress building blocks that make
19	its mathematical core expressible so concisely. Show what the language already
20	gives, what your user-level definitions add, and where a mismatch remains.
21	
22	A correct Python transliteration can be an intermediate check; it is not the
23	destination. TeX-printing that transliteration does not establish mathematical
24	expressiveness. Explore materially different ways to express the computations;
25	do not claim a canonical result after the first working design. You choose the
26	investigative workflow and representations and justify the resulting form.
27	
28	Rendering is an early self-validation gate: render substantive candidate
29	forms, inspect them beside the mathematical formula, and revise before
30	selecting the design. Do not postpone visual fidelity assessment until article
31	production.
32	
33	This is also a concrete test of connecting knowledge of mathematics,
34	transformers and programming languages in an unfamiliar codebase, with
35	inspectable evidence.
36	
37	## Work here, using the already running build
38	
39	You are in a git worktree of an already-built checkout. Do not clone another
40	checkout, reinstall Java/Ant, or rerun baseline suites as onboarding — the
41	baseline is green (clean build; 1,377 testFast; 382 testSystem). Set up once:
42	
43	```sh
44	cp -r /home/user/fortress/ProjectFortress/build $PWD/ProjectFortress/
45	cp -r /home/user/fortress/default_repository $PWD/
46	export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
47	export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
48	export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD
49	unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
50	```
51	
52	Never point `FORTRESS_HOME` at `/home/user/fortress` itself; nothing in the
53	main checkout may be modified. Run probes as
54	`FORTRESS_THREADS=1 ./bin/fortress PATH.fss` (the shared box requires the
55	single-thread setting; the interpreter's subcommandless form walks the file).
56	The Fortress component name must match its filename (sans `.fss`). If library
57	files under your worktree's `Library/` are ever touched, wipe
58	`$PWD/default_repository/caches/*` — but you are not to change the shipped
59	library (see below). If an actual environment failure occurs, report its
60	concrete evidence to the coordinator for repair rather than rebuilding.
61	
62	Create all your work under `experiment/worker/` in your worktree. Keep a
63	command log: append each probe invocation and its captured output to
64	`experiment/worker/transcript.txt` (redirect with `tee -a`). There is no
65	recording wrapper here; the transcript file serves that role.
66	
67	### Rendering pipeline (prepared and verified; do not re-derive it)
68	
69	To typeset actual Fortress source: write a `.tic` file containing the source
70	excerpt, then from its directory:
71	
72	```sh
73	/home/user/fortress/bin/fortick NAME.tic          # .tic -> .tex
74	TEXINPUTS=".:/home/user/fortress/Fortify:" latex NAME.tex
75	dvisvgm --no-fonts --exact-bbox -o NAME.svg NAME.dvi
76	/opt/pw-browsers/chromium --headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu \
77	  --screenshot=NAME.png NAME.svg                  # rasterize to inspect
78	```
79	
80	Inspect the PNG visually and retain the SVG and `.tic` inputs. Delete the
81	`.tex`/`.dvi`/`.aux`/`.log` byproducts. Do not hand-typeset a prettier
82	approximation of the program; render actual source. Plain ASCII alone does
83	not meet the deliverable.
84	
85	## Instruction-following boundary
86	
87	Start from this brief only, with no inherited coordinator conversation. Agents
88	share the filesystem; independence relies on obeying these instructions, not
89	on access restrictions.
90	
91	Do not read, search, recursively list, or otherwise retrieve content from:
92	
93	- `explorations/` — prior experiment work and analysis (any file, any depth).
94	- `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root — it summarizes prior findings.
95	- `experiment/` outside your own `experiment/worker/` — coordinator materials.
96	- Any git branch, ref, log, or historical revision — work with the checked-out
97	  tree only; no `git log`/`show`/`diff` archaeology, which reaches the
98	  excluded material.
99	- GitHub, prior published artifacts, conversation retrieval, or other agents'
100	  findings.
101	
102	Scope searches (grep/glob) to permitted directories explicitly; a repo-wide
103	recursive search includes the excluded paths. Report any accidental exposure.
104	
105	Freely explore this checkout's `Specification/` (TeX sources; no PDFs),
106	`Library/`, `ProjectFortress/`, `Fortify/`, `bin/` and other original source
107	materials. The exclusions restrict contamination, not investigation of
108	Fortress's capabilities.
109	
110	## Design and validation
111	
112	Use Karpathy's original microGPT article and Python source as the behavioral
113	reference: https://karpathy.github.io/2026/02/12/microgpt/ . Pin the actual
114	source revision. If article and gist differ, identify and consistently select
115	a variant. You may download and run the Python locally under
116	`experiment/worker/` to derive deterministic checks (logits/loss/gradients
117	under fixed weights, with justified tolerances); do not commit it anywhere.
118	
119	For each building block, distinguish the mathematical computation from
120	accidents of the Python implementation. Investigate the language's facilities,
121	including reuse, algebraic structure and inference where useful. Do not
122	preselect an operator, type representation, evaluation order or approach from
123	an example. Target recognizable ML notation: where the formula uses ordinary
124	summation, seek that notation. A look-alike glyph or a prettier label in the
125	article does not substitute for an executable definition with the intended
126	meaning.
127	
128	User-level types, operations and library modules are welcome. Do not change
129	the historical language, compiler, runtime or shipped library to make the
130	demo pass. Consult the specification's TeX sources for semantics,
131	source/library for actual behavior, and small probes for evidence. Neither a
132	first interpreter error nor a self-imposed representation proves
133	impossibility; investigate alternatives. Conversely, interpreter acceptance
134	alone does not establish specification conformance. Classify surviving
135	notational departures as an implementation/library gap, language-design
136	limit, or justified design choice, with reproducers and source citations.
137	Retain actionable gaps for the revival worklist without changing the
138	historical system during this experiment.
139	
140	Do not suppress language parallelism merely to reproduce Python's exact
141	order. Distinguish true dependencies, numerical effects and implementation
142	choices. Measure cost honestly, but do not let interpreter speed dictate
143	notation. Keep executions small and bounded; no long training runs.
144	
145	## Deliverables
146	
147	All under `experiment/worker/` in your worktree, mirrored to the session
148	scratchpad directory `blinded-microgpt/` (the coordinator names it in your
149	task message).
150	
151	1. **Running, verified microGPT in Fortress**, including the model,
152	   differentiation, training update and generation path for the pinned
153	   reference, with deterministic logits/loss/gradient checks derived from the
154	   Python reference (never from any prior Fortress solution) and bounded
155	   checks of remaining paths, with justified numerical tolerances.
156	
157	2. **The main educational article and reproducible notation figures.** For
158	   each concept, interleave concise explanation, mathematical formula,
159	   Python, and actual rendered Fortress definition immediately adjacent.
160	   Teach both the transformer and the construction of its notation. Show
161	   supporting definitions and inherited behavior; do not hide machinery to
162	   manufacture apparent brevity. Compare the mathematical core and required
163	   support separately from tests, benchmarks and comments. Explain
164	   substantive alternatives explored and why the chosen form is preferable.
165	   Avoid large code dumps with detached prose. The article is a Markdown
166	   document with the rendered figures beside it; page production happens
167	   after review.
168	
169	3. **A reviewable process record:** meaningful runnable probes including
170	   failures, source versions, command logs, validation data and brief
171	   milestone notes (attempt, observation, decision, uncertainty, evidence
172	   links). These are partial work artifacts, not a full session transcript.
173	   Do not log credentials or dump environment variables.
174	
175	Preserve the independent design and evidence before any comparison with prior
176	work. Subsequent independent review may challenge the solution and
177	investigative claims. The coordinator handles review and eventual comparison.
178	Evaluate results without self-praise or treating this single specimen as
179	proof that coding is solved.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Fortress revival

This is @palimondo's revival of Sun/Oracle's **Fortress** programming language
(Guy Steele's HPC language, 2003–2012; interpreter + partial JVM compiler,
BSD-licensed). The repo carries the full available git history (5397 commits,
root 2007-01-04, HEAD Aug 2012) with pluckyporcupine's Scala 2.10.7/Java 9
migration grafted on top as a tree overlay — see the commit messages of the
graft commits for lineage and attribution. Working mode: Claude explains the
codebase and produces documentation and experiments as we go; Pavol decides
what gets committed. The full collaboration protocol — roles, tone, how work
is presented, commit discipline, delegation — is in
`explorations/protocol.md`; read it at session start.

## Build and run (verified: Ubuntu 24.04 container, JDK 25 — current rung)

```bash
apt-get install -y openjdk-25-jdk-headless ant  # JDK 8/11/17/21 also still work (all gated green)
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export FORTRESS_HOME=<repo root>
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS                          # proxy trust-store options confuse ant's JVM forks
cd $FORTRESS_HOME && ant compileAll              # ~80 s
./bin/fortress explorations/claude_demo.fss      # interpreter ("walk") — this works
```

Toolchain (2026-08-21): Scala 2.13.18 (build.xml drives scalac via
`scala.tools.nsc.Main` directly — Scala 2.13 dropped the `scala.tools.ant`
tasks), ASM 9.10.1 (vendored in
`ProjectFortress/third_party/asm/`; watch out — Fortress's own
`asmbytecodeoptimizer.Opcodes` shadows `org.objectweb.asm.Opcodes` in that
package), `-source/-target 1.8` and emitted classfiles V1_6 (both now
merely conventions — ASM 9 unblocks raising them as a deliberate later
step), sources compiled as UTF-8 (all sources were already valid UTF-8;
the old ISO-8859-1 javac attributes just mis-decoded comments),
work-stealing runtime on stdlib `java.util.concurrent` ForkJoin (vendored
jsr166y retired); see `explorations/modernization-plan.md` for the ladder
and current rung.

Facts that save time:

- **Both execution paths work.** `fortress <file>.fss` interprets directly.
  The bytecode compiler path (`fortress compile` + `fortress run`) also works
  on JDK 8 — pluckyporcupine's "compiled programs don't run" is wrong here —
  but has two traps: imported library components (`System`,
  `CompilerSystem`) must be explicitly `fortress compile`d into the cache
  first, and **stale caches** cause a misleading
  `NoSuchMethodError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println(...)` — wipe
  `default_repository/caches/*` and recompile in library order (recipe in
  `explorations/repo-internals.md`). The compiler is incomplete (some
  constructs still `sayWhat`), not broken. See
  `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`.
- **`ProjectFortress/hello.fss` runs only via the compiler path** — its July
  2012 upgrade imports `System.getProperty`/`CompilerSystem.args`, which the
  interpreter can't resolve. Use `explorations/*.fss` as interpreter smoke
  tests.
- **Test suite (2026-08-19): fully green.** `ant testFast` (~1,400 tests
  incl. the full compiler suite) and `ant testSystem` (382 interpreter
  tests) both pass with zero failures — the first fully green suite in this
  lineage (the 2012 mainline ended with 7 red). History and the two fixes:
  `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`.
- The interpreter requires filename (sans `.fss`) == component name.
- If scalac fails with arity errors in `S*Pattern` nodes, the generated AST
  sources are stale relative to `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`:
  `touch ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast && ant compileAll` regenerates.
- Interpreter caches live in `default_repository/caches/` (gitignored); wipe
  them if library edits seem to have no effect.
- Architecture map, name-resolution rules, cache anatomy, test-harness
  mechanics, and git-archaeology techniques: `explorations/repo-internals.md`
  — read it before diving into the source.

## Layout

- Original Fortress tree: everything not listed below — do not modify
  casually; it is the historical artifact being revived.
- `explorations/` — revival-era experiments and writeups (ours; verified
  running programs).
- `research/` — the Guy Steele corpus: `research/README.md` is a committed
  links-only index; `research/extracts/` holds committed working notes;
  `research/decks/` is **gitignored** (copyrighted PDFs, dropped in per
  session, never committed).
- `Specification/` + `Specification-1.0-frozen/` — the language spec LaTeX
  (in-repo, richer than the published PDF; building it is untested).
